title: How to Use a Retirement Glide Path to Reduce Risk Over Time
description: Automating your asset allocation shift from 'Growth' to 'Safety'.
content:
A 'Glide Path' is the trajectory your asset allocation takes over your lifetime. Typically, it starts high in stocks (e.g., 90%) when you are young and gradually shifts toward bonds (e.g., 50%) as you approach retirement. This reduces the risk of a market crash devastating your portfolio right when you need to spend it. However, getting the glide path wrong—de-risking too early or too late—is costly. This guide explains how to design a custom glide path that balances growth needs with sleep-at-night safety.

Key Takeaways

  • The Accumulation Slope: From age 20 to 50, stay high in equities (80-100%). Volatility is your friend here; it lets you buy cheap shares.
  • The Transition Zone (5 Years Pre-Retirement): This is where the glide path steepens. Shift 5-10% per year into bonds/cash to build a 'Bond Tent' or 'Cash Buffer'.
  • The Landing Point: Determine your 'Retirement Day' allocation (e.g., 60/40). You should hit this target exactly on the day you quit working.
  • Static vs. Rising: Traditional glide paths stay conservative forever. Advanced paths 'Rise' back into equities in late retirement to fight inflation and leave a legacy.

Why It Matters (US Context)

Target Date Funds (TDFs) have a built-in glide path. Understanding whether your TDF is 'To' (most conservative at retirement) or 'Through' (stays aggressive past retirement) is critical. Vanguard TDFs glide 'Through'; BlackRock LifePath typically glides 'To'.

Designing Your Flight Plan

Map your allocation to your age.

Phase 1: The Climb (Age 25-50)

Allocation: 90% Stocks / 10% Bonds.
Goal: Maximize compounding. Ignore volatility.
Glide: Flat. No changes needed.

Phase 2: The Descent (Age 50-65)

Allocation: Shifts from 90/10 to 50/50.
Rate: Move ~2-3% per year into Bonds.
Goal: Reduce 'Sequence of Returns Risk'. You are locking in your career winnings.

Phase 3: The Landing (Age 65-75)

Allocation: 50% Stocks / 50% Bonds (plus 2 years Cash).
Goal: Income stability. You draw from the Bond/Cash side during crashes.

How to Execute the Glide

  1. New Money First: Instead of selling stocks (taxable event), direct 100% of your new contributions in your 50s toward Bonds. This naturally shifts the ratio without triggering taxes.
  2. Dividend Direction: In your 50s, stop reinvesting stock dividends into stocks. Direct them to buy bonds. This is a gentle glide.
  3. The 'One-Time' Rebalance: If you are 5 years from retirement and the market hits an all-time high, seize the moment. Sell 10% of stocks and fill your Cash Bucket. Don't wait for the glide path if the market gives you a gift.
  4. Target Date Funds: The easiest way. Buy a 2035 Fund. It handles the math. You just keep buying.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I stay 100% stocks?

If you have 'Over-Saved' (e.g., you have 50x expenses), yes. You can live off dividends and ignore price drops. But for most, the risk of a 50% drop at age 65 is too scary.

What if rates rise?

Bond prices fall when rates rise. Shorten your bond duration (buy Short-Term Treasuries) during the glide path to minimize interest rate risk.

Is the 'Bond Tent' better?

Research suggests yes. Gliding to a peak bond allocation at retirement (the Tent) and then gliding back to stocks later offers the highest success rate.
